questions.q: What is the primary voice or persona speaking in the two poems of Chapter 14?
questions.a: The primary voice is that of the poet Vadda Gnosoh herself, speaking as an Adivasi woman and representative of her community. A wrong answer might identify "Bafnaza" or "Phako" as the protagonist, revealing confusion between a referenced character and the poetic speaker.

questions.q: Explain in your own words how the speaker's attitude toward her house in the second poem reflects her broader worldview.
questions.a: The speaker wants her house to remain fully open ("पूरी तरह खुला रहे") and not hide, even if it invites danger (darkness, pits). This shows her belief in transparency, fearlessness, and readiness to confront injustice. A wrong answer might focus only on literal architecture, missing the metaphorical defiance.

questions.q: Apply the concept of "poetic persona" to identify two contrasting tones in the first poem (e.g., the description of Bafnaza) and the second poem (the invitation to the house). Provide one line from each poem as evidence.
questions.a: First poem: tone of anguish/outrage at oppression ("बाफ़नज़ा पर लगाम का लगाना... यह मसखरी नहीं" - though the exact line is not quoted, the description says it's not mockery but heartfelt). Second poem: tone of defiant openness ("मेरे घर के द्वार जैसे भोज / अँधेरे को भी देख"). A wrong answer might confuse tone with mood or pick lines that don't contrast.

questions.q: Analyze how the speaker's characterization across both poems constructs a collective Adivasi identity rather than just an individual one.
questions.a: The speaker uses "मेरे घर" (my house) but links it to "पुएफयिड्कत्ज़ु" (Phako) and the community's struggle ("लईवकज लखोकन्ह वकन्क्षयु"). The first poem references "बाफ़नज़ा" as a symbol of the oppressed. The "I" represents the community. A wrong answer would treat the speaker as purely individual, ignoring the collective references.

questions.q: Evaluate whether the speaker's defiance in the second poem ("यदि मैं उसे बुलाऊँ तो कोई आवाज आए") is an act of hope or desperation. Justify with textual evidence.
questions.a: It is an act of hope grounded in collective solidarity: the belief that a call will be answered ("कोई आवाज आए") reflects faith in community response, not isolated desperation. A wrong answer might see it as naive optimism or pure desperation without recognizing the communal assurance.

questions.q: Create a four-line poetic response from the perspective of the speaker's house, personified, reacting to the speaker's demand to stay open.
questions.a: A strong response would personify the house echoing the speaker's resolve (e.g., "I stand unshut, my doors are arms / Embracing night, unafraid of harms / If pits are dug, I'll swallow them deep / My mistress calls, I wake from sleep"). A weak response would be generic or miss the defiant tone.
